Action Plan:
1) Manage likely viral respiratory infection with cough and nasal symptoms via home monitoring and supportive care; escalate if red flags appear or symptoms persist/worsen.
2) Provide symptomatic treatment guidance and daily self-care measures; avoid duplicating paracetamol-containing products; use nighttime cough relief only if needed.
3) Ensure ongoing management of chronic diseases (diabetes and hypertension) with primary care follow-up and routine monitoring.

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: 5 days of cough (dry) and constant nasal discharge; no chest pain, no shortness of breath, no hemoptysis.
- Onset/duration/progression: Symptoms began ~5 days ago and have persisted; no reported improvement.
- Associated signs: Feels hot to touch with chills; no measured fever; no vomiting or diarrhea currently; able to drink fluids; urination okay; no rashes.
- Past medical history: Hypertension; Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
- Allergies: Hay fever (allergic rhinitis) noted.
- Medications: Metformin; Lisinopril (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Social history: Lives with partner and dog; works as office manager; drinks alcohol occasionally; smoking status not documented.
- Other notes: Uses lemon-sips (2–3 per day) for throat irritation; reports some muscle aches; no nosebleeds or ear symptoms; temperature not yet measured at home.

Objective:
- No vitals documented.
- No physical examination findings recorded.
- No imaging or laboratory results available.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute respiratory infection (likely viral) with cough and nasal symptoms; possible chest infection given chest symptoms not prominent but doctor noted concern for chest infection in context of symptoms.
   - Assessment: Acute respiratory infection likely viral; potential bacterial chest infection considered due to diabetes.
   - Differential diagnoses: Viral upper respiratory infection; bronchitis; bacterial pneumonia (less likely at present).
   - Investigations planned: Home temperature measurement; no labs or imaging ordered at this time.
   - Treatment planned: Symptomatic care:
     - Lemsip (paracetamol-containing) for fever/symptoms; avoid concurrent paracetamol-containing products.
     - Cough syrup: not advised for daytime use; may use small amount at night if sleep is affected.
     - Continue lemon sips (2–3 daily) for throat comfort; maintain hydration.
     - Advise monitoring for red flags (see below) and seek follow-up if symptoms worsen or do not settle.
   - Relevant referrals: None at this time.
   - Red flags / follow-up: If fever persists or rises above 37.5–38°C, cough worsens, significant purulent phlegm, hemoptysis, shortness of breath, or chest pain, contact again; antibiotics may be considered if not settling.

2. Diabetes mellitus (type 2)
   - Assessment: Chronic disease present; infection may impact glucose control.
   - Differential diagnoses: None specific beyond status of diabetes.
   - Investigations planned: Continue routine diabetes monitoring with GP; ensure blood glucose and HbA1c monitoring as advised by primary care.
   - Treatment planned: Continue currently prescribed diabetes regimen:
     - Metformin (dose/route/frequency not documented).
     - Lisinopril (dose/route/frequency not documented).
   - Relevant referrals: None.

3. Hypertension
   - Assessment: Chronic hypertension; blood pressure status not recently documented.
   - Differential diagnoses: None.
   - Investigations planned: BP monitoring through GP follow-up; regular BP checks per routine care.
   - Treatment planned: Continue lisinopril (dose/route/frequency not documented); maintain follow-up with GP for BP management.
   - Relevant referrals: None.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements: Allergies to medications (none stated); current medications reconciliation incomplete (doses/routes/frequencies not documented for metformin and lisinopril); smoking status not documented; vital signs not recorded; no physical exam details.
- Internal conflicts: None identified.
- Transcript quality: Some minor ambiguities (smoking status未 documented; exact lisinopril dose) and no objective measurements documented.

Consent and consent-related note:
- Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.
